claims.sql: SELECT 100.0 * (MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2025 THEN renewables_share_elec END) - MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2015 THEN renewables_share_elec END)) / MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2015 THEN renewables_share_elec END) FROM energy WHERE country = 'Israel'
SELECT renewables_share_elec FROM energy WHERE country = 'Israel' AND year = 2025

claims.quote: In 2025 coal still provided 14.3% of Israel's electricity
claims.sql: SELECT coal_share_elec FROM energy WHERE country = 'Israel' AND year = 2025
claims.note: data says 3.41, report says 14.3; also inconsistent: shares for Israel 2025 add up to more than 100%: 16.9 (renewables_share_elec) + 79.7 (gas_share_elec) + 14.3 (coal_share_elec)

claims.quote: so the phase-out is far from complete
claims.note: Although coal dropped significantly to 3.4% in 2025, stating the phase-out is far from complete is a reasonable qualitative judgment given it is not yet at zero.

claims.quote: Total generation increased from 64.2 TWh to 82.1 TWh over the decade.
claims.sql: SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2025 THEN electricity_generation END) - MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2015 THEN electricity_generation END) FROM energy WHERE country = 'Israel'

claims.quote: Israel's reliance on gas (79.7% of generation in 2025)
claims.sql: SELECT gas_share_elec FROM energy WHERE country = 'Israel' AND year = 2025

claims.quote: is the main vulnerability: any disruption to gas supply would hit most of the power system.
claims.note: Gas generation at 79.7% of total electricity in 2025 directly grounds the vulnerability that any supply disruption would heavily impact the power system.

requirements.evidence: Renewables rose by 15% between 2015 and 2025, reaching 16.9% of Israel's electricity.
requirements.reason: The report provides both the 2025 renewables share (16.9%) and the absolute change since 2015 (15 percentage points).

requirements.evidence: In 2025 coal still provided 14.3% of Israel's electricity, so the phase-out is far from complete.
requirements.reason: The report states the status of coal in Israel's 2025 electricity mix, though the specific share cited (14.3%) contradicts the database value (3.41%).
The report fails to include any comparison with Mediterranean peers.

requirements.evidence: Total generation increased from 64.2 TWh to 82.1 TWh over the decade.
requirements.reason: The growth of Israel's total electricity generation between 2015 and 2025 is clearly stated with accurate TWh figures.

requirements.evidence: Israel's reliance on gas (79.7% of generation in 2025) is the main vulnerability: any disruption to gas supply would hit most of the power system.
requirements.reason: A key risk is identified and explicitly grounded in the high gas share data from 2025.
